reviews.review:
Found this by searching through steamdb for obscure games. So many mechanics are clunky and broken (wont play full animation on clicking button, cant roll while walking etc etc), but it sort of adds to the charm. I didnt encounter any combat, so it was basically a walking simulator. A great experience overall though, and definitely worth more than $2 even in its current unfinished and broken state. At least I enjoyed it more than other more expensive games. Got plenty of great laughs. Lots of screenshot-worthy scenes.

Pros: 
-Amazing cozy vibe/environment.
-Quite a bit to explore/look at. The value is not in finding items but in appreciating the vibe/scenery
-Quite funny, both the writing style and the game-breaking bugs
-Day/night cycle, plus rainy weather, although it can switch immediately from night sky to afternoon lighting when it rains.
-Hilariously over-dramatic music when you enter the beach
-Good music overall
-sound design was good i think
-you can hear npcs having conversations 
-There’s a carnival with big hot air balloon flying above
-Beach/coast

Cons: 
-not much interaction/dialogue. I like the dialogue that is present, but it would be great to have more
-I was never able to figure out how to open the inventory, if it even actually exists. Pressed every button/key imaginable but nope.
-mind blowingly crazy keybinds. It’s just not controller-friendly. Had to remap almost everything to play on steam deck. Should also probably only be a single button for interaction. Combining e and f or something
-forced to keep key pressed for some animations to play. it should always play the full animation as soon as the key is clicked
reviews.developer_response: I'm glad you had a good time exploring the world of DarkShine. In the future, we will fix all bugs found during the polishing and refinement stage. Thank you for your feedback.
